AccessTokenResponse.description: Access-token metadata returned by `POST /v4/tokens`, `POST /v4/tokens/openid-connect/authorization-code-flow`, `GET /v4/tokens`, `GET /v4/tokens/{token}`, and `PUT /v4/tokens/exchange/{token}`. Pass `access_token` in the `Authorization` header (`Bearer ...`) on subsequent requests.

access_token.description: Token string. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on subsequent requests, or as the `access_token` query parameter / `extole_token` cookie.

client_id.description: Stable Extole identifier for the client (tenant) this token authenticates against.

expires_in.description: Seconds until this token expires. Once expired, requests using it return `401 invalid_access_token`; rotate via `PUT /v4/tokens/exchange/{token}` before expiry to keep long-lived integrations alive.

identity_id.description: Stable Extole identifier for the identity (user, managed identity, or resource) that this token represents.

person_id.description: Deprecated alias for `identity_id`. New integrations should use `identity_id`.

scopes.description: Authorization scopes granted to this token. Determines which API operations the token may invoke.

items.description: Authorization scopes granted to this token. Determines which API operations the token may invoke.

type.description: Authentication shape backing the token. `USER` represents a human dashboard user, `MANAGED` an OAuth-style managed identity, and `RESOURCE` a scoped per-resource token.

client_domain_id.description: Client domain to build the email against. A real send uses the domain the triggering event arrived on, so name that domain to see the links it produces. Defaults to the client's default domain.

additionalProperties.description: Values the engine would have resolved from the action data map, keyed by data entry name. Available to the email expressions through the context data map. A preview does not evaluate the action data expressions, so an entry left out reads as absent. Defaults to no data.

data.description: Values the engine would have resolved from the action data map, keyed by data entry name. Available to the email expressions through the context data map. A preview does not evaluate the action data expressions, so an entry left out reads as absent. Defaults to no data.

person_id.description: Id of the person the email is built for. The person supplies the values that the email expressions read, such as the recipient address and the first name. Omit it to build the email for the preview person, whose email is preview@example.com and whose first name is preview_first_name. Extole creates that person on the first preview and reuses it after that, so an action is previewable before anyone has entered the journey.

sandbox.description: Sandbox to read the campaign from. Defaults to the campaign sandbox of the campaign being previewed, which holds the latest saved version.

variant.description: Campaign variant to build the email with. A real send evaluates the variant the campaign selected for the person, so name the variant you want to see. Defaults to the first variant the campaign declares, or to en when the campaign declares none.

bcc.description: Addresses the email would be blind copied to.

body.description: HTML body the email would be sent with.

cc.description: Addresses the email would be copied to.

do_not_send_reason.description: Reason this email would not send. Set by the email message expression of the action, or by the opt-out check when the action sends on a checked list and the recipient opted out of it. Absent when neither applies. A send applies suppression rules of its own, such as a bounced or blocked address, which a preview does not evaluate.

from.description: Address the email would be sent from. Absent when the action leaves the from address unset.

additionalProperties.description: Custom email headers the email would be sent with, keyed by header name.

headers.description: Custom email headers the email would be sent with, keyed by header name.

optout_list.description: Opt-out list the email would send on. The promotional and personal lists are checked against the opt-out list. Only the promotional list adds the List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers above.

reply_to.description: Address replies would go to. Absent when the action leaves the reply-to address unset.

subject.description: Subject line the email would be sent with.

to.description: Address the email would be sent to.

recipient.description: Address to send the test email to. The email is built for the person with this address, so the unsubscribe link in the email acts on this address only. Extole creates that person when none exists yet. Required.

variant.description: Campaign variant to build the email with. Defaults to the first variant the campaign declares, or to en when the campaign declares none.

recipient.description: Address the test email is sent to.

send_id.description: Id of the queued send. Pass it as action_id to GET /v2/emails to read the send record and its delivery results once the email service has picked it up.

TargetingAttributesInCampaignControllerT.description: Buildtime expression resolving to a list of event-targeting attribute configurations, combined with logical OR. Each configuration's required key: EVENT_NAME. Optional keys: EVENT_TYPE, PROGRAM, CAMPAIGN, JOURNEY, and APP_TYPE. When EVENT_TYPE is set, supported values are INPUT, STEP, INTERNAL, AUDIENCE_MEMBERSHIP_CREATED, AUDIENCE_MEMBERSHIP_UPDATED, and AUDIENCE_MEMBERSHIP_REMOVED. A configuration whose EVENT_TYPE is an audience membership type instead requires AUDIENCE, the id of the audience, accepts APP_TYPE as its only optional key, and does not accept EVENT_NAME, PROGRAM, CAMPAIGN, or JOURNEY. AUDIENCE is not accepted with any other event type. Buildtime expressions use [ControllerBuildtimeContext](https://github.com/extole/extole-specification/blob/main/openapi/expression-context/com/extole/api/campaign/ControllerBuildtimeContext.d.ts).

info.description:
Advanced configuration endpoints for Extole platform experts: campaign controllers, typed actions and triggers, advanced component types and facets, source mapping, report post-handlers, pre-handlers, and other expert configuration surfaces not included in the standard Management API.

## Updating a resource

`PUT` merges. A field you omit from the body is left at its stored value, so you do not need to read a resource and send it back whole in order to change one field. This is a deliberate departure from the HTTP convention that `PUT` replaces, and it holds across this API.

Two qualifications, both visible on each operation's own request schema:

- Some operations mark fields `required` in their request schema. Those must be sent on every request, whether or not you are changing them.
- A field that holds a list or a map is replaced, not merged, when you supply it. Sending one entry of a collection stores that entry and drops the rest, so to change one member of a collection you must send the collection's other members alongside it.

get.description: Returns all domain pattern definitions for the calling client. Domain patterns define which URL patterns the Extole platform recognises as belonging to this client — they control campaign-tracking domain matching, shareable link generation, and zone-rendering domain allow-listing. Each entry includes its `pattern`, `type` (`GLOB`, `DOMAIN`, or `SUB_DOMAIN`), and the optional `client_domain_id` that links it to a specific program domain configuration.
get.summary: List client domain patterns

post.description: Creates a new domain pattern definition and returns the persisted record with its server-assigned id. The `pattern` field is required. `type` defaults to `GLOB` when omitted. Set `test=true` to create a test-only pattern that is not used in production domain matching. The pattern must be buildable; complex `BuildtimeEvaluatable` expressions are evaluated at build time.

get.description: Returns all domain patterns in their fully evaluated (built) runtime form, with all `BuildtimeEvaluatable` fields resolved to their current string values. Use this when the calling system needs the effective pattern expressions rather than the source template definitions. Use `GET /v1/client-domain-patterns` for the editable source definitions.
get.summary: List built client domain patterns

get.description: Returns the source definition for the supplied domain pattern, including its `pattern` expression, `type`, optional `client_domain_id`, and `test` flag. Returns `400 client_domain_pattern_not_found` if the id does not exist or is not accessible to the calling client. For the compiled runtime snapshot use `GET /v1/client-domain-patterns/{id}/built` instead.

parameters.description: Identifier of the client domain pattern to retrieve.
parameters.name: id

200.description: Client domain pattern source definition with its build-time pattern expression, domain type, and component references.

400.description: The supplied `id` does not match an existing domain pattern for this client. Inspect the response `code` field for the specific error.

get.summary: Get client domain pattern

put.description: Applies a partial update to the supplied domain pattern. Only the fields present in the body are changed; omitted fields are left intact. Returns the updated pattern record on success. Returns `400 client_domain_pattern_not_found` if the id does not exist.

parameters.description: Identifier of the client domain pattern to update.
parameters.name: id

200.description: Client domain pattern source definition with its build-time pattern expression, domain type, and component references.

400.description: The supplied `id` does not match an existing domain pattern for this client. Inspect the response `code` field for the specific error.

delete.description: Soft-archives the supplied domain pattern. Archived patterns are retained but are no longer used in domain matching. Reversible via `POST /v1/client-domain-patterns/{id}/unarchive`. Returns the updated pattern record. Returns `400 client_domain_pattern_not_found` if the id does not exist.

parameters.description: Identifier of the client domain pattern to archive.

get.description: Downloads the binary content of the named asset for the person identified by `personId`. The `name` query parameter selects the asset; omit it to download the person's default asset (if one exists). Returns the asset content stream with the asset's stored content type. Supply `default_url` to redirect to a fallback URL when the asset is not found instead of returning an error. The access token is optional on this operation: omit it and Extole serves only the person's `PUBLIC` assets, resolving the client from the request domain. Supply a token belonging to the person to reach their `PRIVATE` assets. Omitting the token is the recommended way to render another person's avatar, so no token has to be embedded in an image URL.

parameters.description: The Extole unique profile identifier of this user at Extole.
parameters.name: personId

200.description: Binary asset content stream with the asset's stored content type.

400.description: Bad request. The named examples below cover this operation's specific validation errors. Other 400 causes include an invalid access token or a malformed path parameter - inspect the response `code` field for the specific error.

get.summary: Download a person asset by name

get.description: Downloads the binary content of the asset identified by `assetId` for the person identified by `personId`. Returns the asset content stream with the asset's stored content type. If the asset has no downloadable content the server returns 400 with `asset_content_not_downloadable`. Supply `default_url` to redirect the caller to a fallback URL instead of returning an error when the asset is not found. Builds the email the action would send for the given person, without sending it. Evaluates the same expressions the send path evaluates, so the returned subject, body and addresses are what those expressions produce for that person. Reads the action from the campaign sandbox, so an unpublished change is previewable as soon as the campaign builds. A send then applies steps a preview does not: it drops an email whose subject, body, to or from address is blank, it applies opt-out, and it rewrites the from address when the domain is not one the client may send from. So a preview shows the evaluated message, not the decision to deliver it.

Builds the email the action would send and sends it to the given recipient, so it can be checked in a real inbox. The email is built for the person with the recipient address, on the client's default domain, and the action is read from the campaign sandbox, so an unpublished change can be sent as soon as the campaign builds. The cc and bcc addresses of the action are not copied. The send goes through the normal email pipeline, so opt-out, the from address rules and retries apply, and it is recorded like any other send. The action is evaluated once before the send is queued, so an expression that fails is returned as an error by this call. The call returns once the send is queued, not once it is delivered.
